..
As of 140 PM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Heat and humidity persists today across the
south, along with isolated to scattered showers and storms
area-wide late in the day and into tonight.

Early afternoon weather analysis indicated a WNW flow aloft 
with the Bermuda high now getting shunted farther south to the 
Gulf coast and Bahamas. The latest radar indicates two MCSs with
one centered over WV an the other upstream over IN.

With the airmass overturned from yesterday's widespread convection
across VA/MD and the remnant cloud cover from the MCS this
morning, today's SVR potential is highly uncertain. Mesoanalysis
depicted significant CIN across the area early this afternoon.
However, it also shows CIN eroding by late this afternoon. As
such, still think that thunderstorms hold off until late this
afternoon into tonight. CAMs continue to struggle with the
convection which is unsurprising given that there are multiple
MCSs. Therefore, confidence remains low. However, the general
consensus from CAMs is that convection will primarily track SE
into SW VA this afternoon, largely sparing the local area. This
solution does make sense given visible satellite and radar 
which shows the WV MCS diving SSE and a line of storms 
stretching between that MCS and the stronger MCS in IN. Normally
when there is a line of storms ahead of an MCS oriented in a 
direction that the MCS is moving, the MCS ends up tracking along
that line of storms which gives an indication as to where it 
will go. This would line up with CAMs. However, the stronger MCS
in IN is currently tracking north of the NW/SE oriented line of
storms. Therefore, we will have to wait and see if the MCS ends
up tracking along the line of storms (and largely missing the 
local area) or if it ends up tracking a bit north (which could 
bring a higher chance for severe storms to the local area late 
this afternoon into tonight). Will also note that there may be 
enough clearing across SE VA/NE NC for additional storm 
development (similar to what happened yesterday). Given the 
uncertainties, have PoPs gradually increasing into this evening 
with the highest PoPs between 8 PM and 2 AM (30-45%).

SPC has locations generally west of I-95 in a slight (level 2/5)
risk for severe storms today with the rest of the area under a
marginal risk (level 1/5). The main threat is damaging winds
given seasonably strong shear of 25-35 kt and high DCAPE (1000
J/kg along and south of the VA/NC border). In addition, a 
marginal ERO is in effect for most of the region (with a Slight
nudging into the far NW). Have maintained a small Heat Advisory
for the interior NE NC zones along the Albemarle sound where 
sfc dew pts should be several degrees higher, along with highs 
into the mid 90s, leading to heat indices of 105+ for a few
hours. However, temps and dew points (especially temps) are 
lower than model guidance given the overturned airmass and
lingering clouds/stability. As such, confidence in reaching Heat
Advisory criteria has decreased. However, given the clearing
occuring in NE NC, will continue the Heat Advisory for now in
case conditions are reached later this afternoon. Elsewhere, 
highs will generally be in the upper 80s to lower 90s with heat
indices in the mid 90s to around 100F. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...An unsettled pattern continues through the 
remainder of the week, trending to a cooler and somewhat drier 
start to the weekend. However, uncertainty remains high.

WNW flow aloft continues Wed through the remainder of the week 
as a ridge aloft is expected to continue through late in the 
week as an upper level ridge builds across the central CONUS, 
and eventually shifts E-SE across the deep south. Meanwhile, a 
trough lingers across New England and eastern Canada. Expect an 
active pattern with the daily potential for isolated to 
scattered storms each afternoon/evening. 

SPC has maintained a marginal risk (level 1/5) for severe storms 
across southern portions of the FA Wed. However, confidence 
continues to remain low given uncertainty in aforementioned MCS
timing and impacts. For now, have largely kept NBM PoPs 
(30-35% SW to 15-25% NE) to account for the potential for 
isolated to scattered storms. Beyond Wed, the pattern remains 
similar with mostly only a slight chance (15-25%) for a few 
isolated showers or storms on Thu (and only general thunder 
risk) with a better chance on Fri (30-40% PoPs). Outside of 
convection, temps remain near the warm side of normal with highs
in the upper 80s to lower 90s Wed and Thu and upper 80s to 
lower 90s Fri.
